title: LinkedIn Native Image Upload: 200% More Impressions | vitalii.no
description:
Why a properly uploaded image beats a link preview on LinkedIn, and how to automate the five-step API dance behind it.

Default LinkedIn link previews are small, blurry and outside your control, and they pull two to three times fewer impressions than a native image. Doing it properly means walking LinkedIn's multi-step API by hand for every post: register the asset, get an upload URL, stream the binary data, retrieve the URN, then create the UGC post. That is a non-starter inside an automated content pipeline.

A post-to-linkedin Supabase Edge Function written in Deno now orchestrates the whole flow. It first calls wasAlreadyPosted() against the posts table, checking both posted and pending statuses, which closes the race condition that used to cause double posts. It then runs the upload handshake with the LinkedIn Assets API, downloads the source image, streams the bytes, and builds the final UGC post with the returned asset URN. If the image upload fails at any point, the function degrades gracefully to an ARTICLE-type post so the content still ships as a link preview.

Average impressions per post rose by over 200 percent with native uploads, and the duplicate-prevention check eliminated the double-posting bug entirely.
